newsitem.title: FRANCE: Club Med dives into loss, restructures.
newsitem.headline: Club Med dives into loss, restructures.

text.p: French leisure and holiday group Club Mediterranee said on Friday it had decided on a drastic restructuring which would cost 820 million francs ($144.1 million) along with other charges, resulting in a net group loss of 743 million francs for the year to October 31, 1996.
The group made a profit of 169 million the previous year.

The group, whose shares were suspended on the Paris Bourse on Friday morning, issued a statement after the stock market closed, saying the board had approved the accounts and the changes in the group.

It said Euro Disney boss Philippe Bourguignon would be moving to Club Med to take up the post of chief executive and that current chairman Serge Trigano would be made head of a supervisory board at Club Med.
Turnover in the year came in at 8.005 billion francs, roughly the same as last year at constant exchange rates and structure, it said.

The statement said the results of the second half of the financial year had shown a break with the improving trend that had followed losses in 1993, reflecting worse market conditions and increased competition and resulting pressure on margins.

"Confronted with this situation, the Club has decided to take a certain number of corrective measures, especially in Europe, aimed at better matching its product offer on two ranges, Club Med and Club Aquarius, to the level and profile of the demand as it exists today," said the statement.
"This situation had prompted the chairman to propose a drastic restructuring plan...with the aim of restoring group profitability," it added. ($ = 5.691 French Francs)
